newsitem.title: HUNGARY: WARNER STARTS MUSIC TELEVISION IN HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: WARNER STARTS MUSIC TELEVISION IN HUNGARY.

text.p: Time-Warner's Warner Music Group> (WMG) said on Friday it was starting a Hungarian language music television station in Hungary.
"We have all the ingredients to start a successful music channel, (but) the key ingredient is to reach local audiences," Stanley Fertig, WMG Vice-President told Reuters.
"It is no longer feasible to produce such programmes in the U.S. and spread them around the world".
The channel, Z+, distributed cost-free through cable, will go live on Friday and would reach an estimated 700,000 of Hungary's 3.9 million households.
Fertig said it was difficult to judge when the station would reach the break-even point but that it would not be in the first or second year.
The station will broadcast 122 hours a week and initially their programme will have a 25 percent domestic music videos but the company plans to increase that ratio to 35 percent.
Fertig said that although the channel will not produce music videos, its existence was likely to encourage the production of those.
The company plans to distribute the programme in neighbouring countries with Hungarian minorities such as Romania or Slovakia.
WMG, together with local partners, also operates Germany's Viva music channel and Channel V in Asia.
